Hmm, in the isosceles case, for OM=ON we need O on the perpendicular bisector of MN, which is the axis of symmetry. If β=γ then by symmetry there's a solution with K↔L swapped; but the claim "the configuration is symmetric precisely when β=γ" — actually if the configuration is symmetric then β=γ by reflecting the angle conditions. And O is the circumcentre of AKL; reflection swaps K and L and fixes A, so the circumcircle maps to itself, O fixed, so O on the bisector, and M,N are swapped by reflection, hence OM=ON.
